newsitem.title: USA: MTV, Intel join in new interactive feature.
newsitem.headline: MTV, Intel join in new interactive feature.

text.p: Music Television (MTV), a unit of Viacom Inc, and Intel Corp plan to begin offering a new interactive broadcast feature for popular music fans on April 11, the companies said on Monday.
The feature, called Intercast Jam, will allow viewers of the MTV cable channel and its M2 sister network to watch broadcast music videos on their personal computers.
At the same time, the Intel technology enables viewers to read news, biographical information and tour and album data, among other things, about the artist featured in the video being broadcast.
MTV will offer the Intel technology two hours a day during its music video programs, while M2 will begin round-the-clock Intercast programming.
The MTV-Intel link is part of an earlier deal between the two companies, which includes on-air and online advertising.

Separately, Gateway 2000 Inc said it would make Intel's Intercast technology available on some models of its desktop PCs beginning April 14. Gateway said it planned to promote its Intercast-enabled personal computers through on-air advertising and product placement on MTV.
